title: One-Pass SCT-Like Authenticated Encryption
summary: SCT uses two passes, which some applications may not tolerate; designing a similar one-pass mode with OAE online nonce-misuse resistance remains open.

formal_statement.body: SCT relies on two passes, which some applications may not tolerate. The open task is to design an authenticated-encryption mode similar to $\mathrm{SCT}$ that uses only one pass while achieving online nonce-misuse resistance in the $\mathrm{OAE}$ sense.

scope.domain: Design of SCT-like authenticated-encryption modes with online nonce-misuse resistance.
parameters: Pass count: a processing constraint fixed at one for the sought mode, versus two for SCT
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct an SCT-like one-pass authenticated-encryption mode achieving online nonce-misuse resistance in the OAE sense.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents this as a future-work direction motivated by applications that cannot tolerate SCT's two passes. It seeks an SCT-like one-pass mode with online nonce-misuse resistance in the OAE sense.
citation_labels: Thomas Peyrin et al., Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers
